html:
A coastal town in southeastern Togo, founded in the late 17th century by Ga and Fante people from the Gold Coast, known to European traders as Little Popo.

It was a port of the Atlantic slave trade and later of palm oil, and Afro-Brazilian and Ga merchant families such as the Lawsons grew powerful there. Its people, the Guin or Mina, gave their name to a language of the coast. When the Germans took the coast in 1884 they first ruled the colony from Aneho, until they moved the capital to Lome in 1897. See also German Togoland and Vodun.
